summary: Session 2 of 3 complete. Delivered the data-load half of generate-migration on the shared resolved-schema model. Refactored Session 1's SqlServerDdlGenerator into MigrationSchemaResolver (single authority on surviving columns/types/identity/PK + real enforced-FK edges + all degradations) and SqlServerDdlEmitter (pure text); GenerateDdl now delegates and the DDL output is byte-identical (all 52 Session-1 DDL tests + fixture stop-rule tests stayed green). New: TableDependencyOrderer (FK-safe load order via Tarjan SCC + deterministic Kahn over the condensation; only true multi-table SCCs flagged ForeignKeyCycle, descendants of a cycle still load after it; self-loops ignored); CsvTableReader (RFC 4180; unquoted-empty=NULL vs quoted-empty=''; documents + pins the real CsvWriter ''->NULL collapse); SqlValueFormatter (typed INSERT literals by DAO type with '-escaping, bit/date/guid quoting, binary flagged not-loadable); SqlServerDataLoadGenerator (INSERTs from the sanitized CSV in FK-safe order, SET IDENTITY_INSERT ON/OFF when the identity column is loaded, binary/OLE + missing-file + missing-column flagged DataColumnOmitted/MissingDataFile, never fabricated); SqlServerMigrationGenerator combinator (DDL + order + data + merged byte-stable degradations). IDENTITY framing keys off the identity column actually being present in the INSERT set (preserve-vs-remap was decided upstream by sanitize and is already baked into the CSV per plan section 5). Build green; AccessHarvester.Pipeline.Tests = 777 hermetic tests (0 failed, 0 skipped), incl. 93 Migration cases. Cross-provider verification: gpt-5-4 R1 ISSUES_FOUND (2 Major: cycle fallback misordered non-cycle descendants; NULL-vs-empty contract unproven against the real producer) -> both fixed in-session (Tarjan SCC + condensation ordering with a cycle-plus-downstream regression test; documented + pinned the real ''->NULL collapse via a real-CsvWriter round-trip test) -> R2 VERIFIED, no regressions.

reason.specifics: Session 3 (generate-migration CLI subcommand + manifest, end-to-end emit against a committed fixture with a hermetic golden-script test, interpretation/install guide updates, ROADMAP/change-log, closeout + Step 9 reorg) is mechanical integration + docs + closeout synthesis. A routed analysis (gemini-pro) recommends Sonnet at medium effort: Opus would be overkill, change-log prose routes to summarization (max_tier=1) regardless. Session 3 consumes SqlServerMigrationGenerator.Generate(inputs, openTableCsv) and emits the manifest from its merged degradation list.

post_close_resolutions: Known limitation (out of Session-2 scope, verifier-agreed not mandatory): the sanitize CsvWriter emits both SQL NULL and a genuine empty string as an unquoted empty field, so the migration data-load loads an empty field as NULL (the '' -> NULL collapse is documented in CsvTableReader and pinned by a real-writer round-trip test). If preserving genuine empty strings end-to-end becomes a product requirement, change the producer (quote empty strings or use a NULL sentinel) as separate sanitize-tier follow-up work.
